defects.summary: Prior Windows-estate P0: three dapi tokens in C:/Users/Prekzursil/.claude/event-ledger/GitHub-f0c32f04/events.jsonl:420-423. On this Linux worktree that ledger path does not exist (ledger_exists=false; tier_B_count=0). This unit did not rotate or print any credential. The finding is not an open P0 on the corpus that this worktree can see.

DETECTOR CAPABILITY GAP with a known root cause, program-wide relevance. gitleaks 8.30.1's default aws-access-token rule constrains the trailing 16 characters to [A-Z2-7] (base32: no 0, 1, 8 or 9) instead of the canonical [A-Z0-9]. Measured consequence: only 44/241 = 0.1826 of canonical-shape AWS access key ids are reported here, 0.1600 of 500 on the cross-vendor refuter's independent sample, against a closed-form expectation of (32/36)^16 = 0.1519. The base32 predicate separates fired from missed with 100% accuracy (44/0/196/0) on this unit's labels. CONSEQUENCE: any gate in this program that reads a clean gitleaks run as proof of no-AWS-credential carries an ~85% blind spot for that shape, and a REAL leaked key is more likely to be missed than caught. Mitigation available today: pair gitleaks with a shape-specific regex sweep over the vendor prefixes that matter -- exactly what this unit's independent dapi regex did when it out-counted gitleaks 12 to 4 on the live exposure.

This unit's own instruments carried three defects, all found before reporting and all corrected in-flight: C1 a path-normalisation bug that reported gitleaks recall as 0.0 (caught because the same run listed the canary rule names -- a self-contradiction); C2 two malformed canaries (CAN-13, CAN-17) that measured nothing about the detector and would have inflated the reported FN rate; C3 an entropy recall of 1.0 that was a +/-8-line proximity artefact against a 53k-hit scanner, corrected to 0.55 by exact token-hash matching. Recorded rather than deleted, per the program's overclaim-retirement rule.

recall_summary.why_entropy_recall_is_low: The entropy scanner's 4.0 bits/char threshold structurally cannot flag a pure-hex token: 16 symbols cap Shannon entropy at exactly log2(16) = 4.0. That is why it did NOT independently isolate the real Databricks tokens (dapi + 32 hex, measured 3.861 bits/char) -- a design flaw in PROBE 1b, disclosed rather than buried. The real exposure was found by githeaks' vendor rule and corroborated by a shape-specific regex, not by entropy.

corrections_applied.C3_line_window_artefact: entropy recall by +/-8-line window = 1.0; by exact token hash = 0.55. The window figure is WITHDRAWN as a proximity measurement.
